scope_statement: Mechanical discovery only. No runtime code, no semantic inference, no M10/M11 change, no existing M12 record change, no Git write. Nothing here promotes a candidate or closes M12; only Sol may make that decision.

queries_performed.detail: Repo-wide text scan for exact occurrences of 9 behavior identities and 5 target SkillIDs (3339 files, 456,891,213 bytes).
Read-only schema+row-count dump of all 43 tables in data/db/hsr_content_4.4.54.sqlite.
LIKE scan of every *_json column in all 43 tables for 12 behavior/ability terms (AbilityName, EntryAbility, AbilityList, _Phase, SkillTriggerKey, AbilityID, ...).
Parsed 2405 JSON files and walked 1,897,439 JSON objects looking for any object containing both a skill-id key and an ability-name key.
Same walk, measuring (a) SkillID + Skill<label> in one object, (b) Skill<label> key + ability-name value in one object, (c) SkillID + Name=Skill<label> in one object.
For each of the 5 audited candidates, listed every file containing BOTH the numeric SkillID and the named behavior string, and extracted the enclosing JSON object.
Compared the label hypothesis (SkillID -> SkillTriggerKey -> CharacterConfig.SkillList[].Name -> EntryAbility) against the same-index hypothesis for Natasha (1105) and Black Swan (1307).
Extended Q6 to all 91 AvatarConfig rows / 620 AvatarConfig SkillList entries against every owner CharacterConfig.
SHA-256 of 6693 files; compared the declared Natasha digest against every file; tested CRLF/LF normalization; read Git blob identity at the producing commit.
git ls-files / log / log --full-history / show / rev-parse / hash-object / config for the Natasha artifacts. No write command was issued.
Per-candidate exact static field inventory from the Nanoka 4.4.54 skills table.
Extracted declared vs path version labels for every artifact cited.

natasha_hash_reconciliation.classification_basis: The git blob is byte-identical between the producing commit and HEAD, and the working tree is clean, so the JSON content has never changed. The declared digest is exactly the SHA-256 of the same file's bytes with CRLF normalized to LF; the working-tree copy is pure CRLF (270 CRLF, 0 bare LF) because core.autocrlf=true. The 8,930-byte LF form and the 9,156-byte CRLF form are the same document.
natasha_hash_reconciliation.why_the_ledger_flagged_a_mismatch: The M12 ledger hashed the working-tree (CRLF) bytes for this file while its recorded hashes for the sibling artifacts match that file's raw bytes; the ledger therefore mixed normalisation conventions between files, which produced a false PROVENANCE_DIGEST_MISMATCH.
natasha_hash_reconciliation.repair_note: The declaration was not rewritten and no file was modified, per this change request's scope.

reentry_detail: Three mechanically proven items and one declaration finding are new: the digest mismatch is a serialization artifact (NE-1), the same-index shortcut is disproven (NE-2), the audited candidates disagree with the explicit EntryAbility field (NE-3), and the missing edge is a single undeclared cross-table equivalence that already exists in declared form for the monster family (NE-4). None of these is a promoted exact join and none closes a REF02 field, so this change request does not assert that M12 is unblocked.
